narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='m1'/>The centre cannot be a corner, so only places on the circle can be corners.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>But the centre is allowed, and the lines from it are the easiest equal sides.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Leaving it out hides the best triangles.
removed_beats.on_screen: the slip's bubble shows a triangle with all three corners on the circle and the centre crossed out; the bubble is struck through

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>To check, measure the two lines from the centre with the ruler.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>They match, so the triangle has two equal sides.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Your turn. Can the centre and one place on the circle ever make a triangle by themselves?
removed_beats.on_screen: the stage clears except the anchor; the words two radii are equal appear

old_misconception.wrong_answer: the centre cannot be a corner
old_misconception.wrong_move: A common slip leaves the centre out, but the centre gives two equal radii for free.
